cover_sub: Explore the financial health data across the nonprofit sector.

slides.label: Operating Reserves
slides.headline: 40% of nonprofits with limited reserves
slides.body: Approximately 40% of nonprofits have fewer than 3 months of operating reserves, indicating financial vulnerability.

slides.label: Small Organizations
slides.headline: Small orgs invest directly in programs
slides.body: Small nonprofits under $500K are more likely to have lean reserves, but this is due to direct investment in their programs.

slides.label: Funding Paradox
slides.headline: More orgs, less funding per organization
slides.body: Despite the increase in the number of nonprofits, average funding per nonprofit has declined by 3 percent.

slides.label: Vulnerability
slides.headline: Small organizations particularly vulnerable
slides.body: Smaller organizations are disproportionately affected by the decrease in average funding, further straining their financial health.

slides.label: Data Gap
slides.headline: Funders lack data on impact
slides.body: Funders often lack the necessary data to determine where their funding will have the most significant impact, affecting the sector's overall health.

slides.label: Data Source
slides.headline: Data from public IRS 990 filings
slides.body: All the data presented here comes from public IRS 990 filings, offering a transparent and accurate snapshot of the nonprofit sector's financial health.
